Final categorization: EXCLUDED  
(Justification: The paper is a non-review research article whose primary focus is on predicting species extinctions and biodiversity impacts due to hydropower development, not on land use/land cover (LULC) prediction itself. While it uses projected forest loss from dam construction as input (e.g., estimating hectares of forest submerged or disturbed), this LULC change is derived from engineering and project data—not from a spatially explicit LULC modeling framework with scenarios, accuracy metrics, or mapped LULC projections as outputs. The study does not implement LULC prediction models; instead, it adopts deforestation estimates from prior work (Pandit et al. 2007) and project-specific data to feed into a species–area relationship (SAR) model. It fails core inclusion criteria: (1) no national-scale spatial LULC modeling is conducted—the analysis is focused on river basins in the Indian Himalaya (a regional subset of India); (2) LULC prediction is not the primary objective but a secondary input; (3) no quantitative accuracy metrics for LULC change are reported; and (4) outputs are species extinction projections, not mapped LULC futures. Additionally, the geographic scope is regional (Indian Himalayan basins), not national-scale across all of India, violating the explicit national-scale requirement. Thus, it meets exclusion criteria: “Local/regional... scale focus” and “Species-specific/ecological focus unrelated to LULC [prediction as primary goal].”)
